reading.text:
Reading of def:Dissertation.Law.lawP2.

Paper notion. Law(Theta) in P_2(S) of a square integrable random element Theta (Def. 2.2:
"(Theta, Law(Theta)) ... Theta in L^2(Omega, F_t; H) together with its own law mu =
Law(Theta) in P_2(H)"; rho = Law(X_T); mu_t = Law(Theta_t)). Law(Theta) := P o Theta^{-1}.

Faithful Lean definition: lawP2 P Theta (possibly with proof arguments AEMeasurable/AEStrongly
Measurable Theta and square integrability, or MemLp Theta 2 P) := the element of P2 S with
underlying measure Measure.map Theta P. If lawP2 is total with a junk value (e.g. delta_0 or
some fixed element) when Theta is not square integrable / not measurable, then it is faithful on
the paper's domain (all paper laws are of L^2 random elements, at least for a.e. t), and the junk
branch must not be relied on: in particular, for law flows t |-> Law(Theta_t) evaluated at times
where Theta_t is not in L^2 (a Lebesgue-null set of t for Z, U), a junk value is harmless only if
every use is dt-a.e. or time-integrated (the paper: "every claim made about them is dt-a.e. or
time-integrated"). Must use the base probability measure P of the standing space and the Borel
sigma-algebra on S. Law of a.e.-equal random elements must coincide.

comparison.text:
def:Dissertation.Law.lawP2 (Dissertation/Law/LawP2.lean:66-76):
  lawP2 P Θ := if h : MemLp Θ 2 P then ⟨P.map Θ, …⟩ else P2.dirac 0   (F Borel, P probability).
Against the reading:
- On the paper's domain (Θ ∈ L²(Ω; F), i.e. MemLp Θ 2 P: a.e. strongly measurable with
  E‖Θ‖² < ∞) the value is the image measure P ∘ Θ⁻¹ (lawP2_law). Matches Law(Θ).
- Off L² the value is the junk δ₀ (lawP2_of_not_memLp). The paper never takes laws of non-L²
  elements except, for law flows, possibly on Lebesgue-null sets of times (Z_t, U_t), where the
  paper itself uses Borel representatives and only dt-a.e. or time-integrated claims; the junk is
  harmless there provided the specs use it only in such a.e./integrated ways (a question for the
  propositions, not this definition).
- MemLp requires AEStronglyMeasurable; on the paper's separable spaces this is AEMeasurable, and
  in general it matches the paper's Bochner space L²(Ω; H). Base measure: the P passed in.
- a.e.-equal random elements have the same lawP2 (lawP2_congr).
Verdict: faithful with representation choices (total function with junk δ₀ off L²).

verdict.detail:
lawP2 is total: for Θ ∈ L²(Ω;F) (MemLp Θ 2 P) its value is the image measure P∘Θ⁻¹, the paper's
Law(Θ); otherwise it is the junk value δ₀. The paper only forms laws of square-integrable elements
(Definition 2.2, ρ = Law(X_T), μ_t for a.e. t), so on the paper's domain the definition is exact.
The junk can only be reached at times where Θ_t ∉ L², a Lebesgue-null set for the paper's tuples,
where the paper too uses arbitrary Borel representatives. Uses that depend on it would have to be
judged in the propositions.
